blocks.body: TC-04 and TC-07 taught the signal path and a first bench. This lab adds the controls and the station wiring those labs left out: AGC, RIT, scanning, a keyer, a hotspot, mobile DC power, and what a receiver is actually doing. You still do not need a radio in the room.

Look at a mobile power path on a diagram, a digital hotspot next to a repeater, and a coax cable cut open. An SWR meter and an RF power meter belong in the feed line, and the meter has to be rated for the frequency and power you will use. Flat copper strap is the preferred RF bonding conductor. A computer sound connection, or a digital interface, is what ties a computer to the radio for a digital mode.

Drop a signal until only the more sensitive receiver still copies it. Follow a mixer and a transverter on a block diagram. Read 1:1 and 4:1. Then take a neighbor's interference report apart with evidence.

observations.label: Transmit into a dummy load
observations.detail: The neighbor's broadcast radio goes quiet when you transmit into the dummy load. The energy was leaving through the antenna.

observations.label: Listen on a nearby handheld
observations.detail: Your FM audio sounds clean on a receiver tuned to your frequency. You are not hearing splatter.

observations.label: Look at the neighbor's radio
observations.detail: It is a small broadcast receiver a few meters from your antenna. It plays your voice only while you transmit.

actions.label: Work with the neighbor on separation or a filter at their receiver

blocks.prompt: Why should you identify where a problem enters a system before deciding what equipment needs to be changed?
blocks.reference: A dark symptom has more than one front door. High SWR, a thin power wire, a neighbor's overloaded receiver, and too much microphone gain can all sound like 'the radio is bad.' The dummy load, the SWR reading, the local monitor, and the control you just moved each test a different door. Replacing a box before you know which door the problem used wastes the part and can leave the fault in the station.

blocks.body: Radio Lab practice for the station work in this lab. Not the official pool.

questions.stem: You turned AGC on and a loud station stopped blasting over a weak one. What did the control do?
choices: It reduced receiver gain when the signal was strong
It raised transmitter power
It changed the repeater offset
questions.why: AGC evens the audio by turning the gain down for strong signals. It is not a power or offset control.

questions.stem: A station answers your CQ and the voice pitch sounds high. Which control moves the receiver a little and leaves the transmit frequency alone?
choices: RIT
The scan button
The keyer
questions.why: Receiver incremental tuning shifts only the receive frequency. Scanning hunts through memories. A keyer times Morse from a paddle.

questions.stem: What did this lab say a DMR code plug is for?
choices: Storing channels, color codes, and talkgroups
Increasing the supply voltage
Measuring SWR
questions.why: The code plug is configuration. Selecting a talkgroup chooses the group of stations. It is not a meter and not a power supply.

questions.stem: Which description matches the hotspot in this lab?
choices: A low-power access point that links nearby radios into a network
Another name for any hilltop repeater
The shield of a coaxial cable
questions.why: A hotspot serves nearby radios and a network. A repeater retransmits over a service area. They can both carry digital voice and still be different stations.

questions.stem: On the mobile diagram, where did the fuse belong?
choices: In the positive lead, close to the battery
Only at the radio, so the long cable stays unfused
In the antenna shield
questions.why: A short in the cable has to open a fuse before the wire can heat. The fuse near the battery does that. The negative return still goes to the battery, and the power wires stay short and heavy.

questions.stem: The classroom signal is weak. One receiver copies it and another does not. What ability is that?
choices: Sensitivity
The SWR of the microphone
DTMF
questions.why: Sensitivity is detecting a weak signal. Selectivity is separating signals. A mixer shifts frequency. A transverter moves the radio to another band. The scale in the lab is not a laboratory measurement.

questions.stem: The model shows 1:1, then 4:1. What should you take from those two readings?
choices: 1:1 is a match and 4:1 is a large mismatch that can make a radio reduce power
Both readings are perfect matches
4:1 is the one safe number for every radio
questions.why: 1:1 means the impedances match in this model. 4:1 is a serious mismatch. Many solid-state radios fold back as SWR rises. Lost feed-line power becomes heat. The lab does not publish one protection threshold for all equipment.

questions.stem: The neighbor's broadcast radio hears you, a dummy load makes that stop, and a handheld on your frequency hears clean audio. What is the fitting next step?
choices: Treat it as overload of their receiver and work with them
Replace your transmitter before any check
Decide the report cannot be real
questions.why: The checks did not show a dirty transmitter. A strong fundamental can overload a nearby consumer radio. You still respond. You do not assume either station is at fault before the evidence.

blocks.body: Mobile and home station diagnostic. Inspect the power path, the settings, the feed line, the SWR, the receiver, and an interference report. Choose the next action from the evidence.

config.doneText: Each next action followed the observation that pointed to it.

cases.prompt: The mobile radio gets hot and quiet on transmit. The supply wires are short and heavy, and the fuse is intact.

observations.label: Read the SWR
observations.detail: The meter in the feed line shows 4:1. The radio's output has dropped.

actions.label: Inspect the feed line, connectors, and antenna
Replace the radio without looking at the line

cases.prompt: Stations on the repeater say your audio drops out when you talk loudly. The SWR on a dummy load is fine.

observations.label: Read the report again
observations.detail: The failure is on voice peaks. The repeater is accepting the signal the rest of the time.

cases.prompt: A neighbor on another band hears your transmissions. You have not checked your own station yet.

observations.label: Listen on the other band
observations.detail: A receiver there hears you while you transmit.

observations.label: Transmit into a dummy load
observations.detail: The other-band receiver goes quiet. The energy was leaving the antenna.

actions.label: Check your station for energy outside the frequency you meant to use
Tell the neighbor their receiver is the only possible cause

blocks.body: These checks were stated or skipped. Each one has to be used.
